candidate_windows.window_text: As mentioned in Section 5.1, we arrange the training data in small groups of size $n$ , in which hypotheses from the same source are put together. In our experiment, $n = 4$ , so the number of rank loss computations within one group is $\binom{n}{2} = \binom{4}{2} = 6$ .
We run all of our experiments on a single NVIDIA A100 40GB GPU. We report the training and testing time in Table 10.

We repeat our experiments five times with different random seeds for training the models. We report the $F_{0.5}$ scores in Table 11 and report the mean and standard deviation in Table 12. Table 10: Running time of each process on a single NVIDIA A100 40GB GPU.
